hints: Each new cube goes on the tower whose top is the smallest value strictly greater than the cube.
If no tower top is greater, start a new tower.
A sorted list of tower tops makes this the first value greater than x.
analogy: Place each cube onto the smallest taller top; this leaves other tower tops as low as possible.
example: For cubes 3,8,2,1,5, tops evolve to [3], [3,8], [2,8], [1,8], [1,5], so two towers.
algorithm: Maintain tower top values in sorted order. For each x, binary-search the first top>x and replace it; if absent, append a new top.
correctness: The rule uses an available compatible tower whenever possible and changes its top to x; every tower must correspond to an increasing subsequence of placed tops, so the count is minimal.
complexity: O(n log n) time and O(n) space.
